title: SpiffeId::uri() interpolates unvalidated trust domain and path, allowing authority injection
description:
EXPLOITABLE when combined with persona-5s4b.30 (unverified OIDC payload); hygiene otherwise.

persona-core/src/spiffe_id.rs:87-89 builds the URI by raw interpolation with no validation, escaping, or percent-encoding of either component:
    format!("spiffe://{}/{}", self.trust_domain, self.path)
SpiffeId::new (spiffe_id.rs:79-84) accepts any String for path, and TrustDomain::OrgOidc(String) (spiffe_id.rs:36) accepts any String as the URI authority.

TRIGGER: persona-attestors/src/oidc.rs:87-90 feeds both from an unverified token payload:
    SpiffeId::new(TrustDomain::OrgOidc(extract_domain(&iss)), format!("user/{sub}/via/oidc-cached"))
extract_domain (oidc.rs:45-51) only strips the scheme and trailing slash; it does not reject path, query, fragment, userinfo or port content. So iss = "https://good.example/x" yields authority "good.example/x" and the URI spiffe://good.example/x/user/.../via/oidc-cached.

CONSEQUENCE:
1. Authority confusion. Any conformant parser - including this crates own SpiffeId::from_str (spiffe_id.rs:125), which splits at the FIRST slash - reads that ID as trust domain "good.example" with path "x/user/...". An attacker controlling iss injects arbitrary paths underneath a trust domain they do not own. A relying party whose rule is "trust domain == good.example" accepts it.
2. Variant confusion on round trip. parse_trust_domain (spiffe_id.rs:143-157) reconstructs variants by string prefix, so OrgOidc("personal.evil") parses back as PersonalDid("evil") and OrgOidc("piv.evil") as PivIssuer("evil") - an attacker-supplied iss of https://piv.evil promotes itself into the smart-card issuer namespace.
3. sub is equally unconstrained: sub = "x/via/tailscale" injects a fake provenance segment into the path that provenance() (spiffe_id.rs:95-101) parses structurally.

Fix direction: validate at construction per SPIFFE spec - trust domain restricted to lowercase DNS-name characters with no /, ?, #, @ or :, and path segments restricted and percent-encoded. Return a typed error instead of building a malformed URI. Rejecting bad input here also contains persona-5s4b.30 to a single trust domain.
close_reason: Implemented in 4698b8a. Claim moved to its own module with private fields; enumerate returns Candidate, prove returns Evidence, Claim::derive is fallible so no evidence means no claim and the daemon declines. All three acceptance criteria verified by execution. .55 fixed by construction: SelfAssertedDomain has no OrgOidc variant, so oidc.rs cannot anchor a trust domain from an unverified iss.
